cards.explanation: The singing is for the glory of God's name. The psalm says it plain: "Sing the glory of His name; make His praise glorious." The whole earth is in the choir, friends, and God's name is the song. That's what the singing is for.
The word is cower. The psalm says, "So great is Your power that Your enemies cower before You." That's what happens when someone's power is that big. Nobody is strutting in that room.

The answer is False. The words the psalm gives the earth say, "All the earth bows down to You; they sing praise to You; they sing praise to Your name." Not a few nations, not half. All the earth, singing it twice.

God turned the sea into dry land, friends. The psalm says, "He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot…" People crossing a sea on foot. I can't even hop across my own bakery without wondering if my gold base is going to catch a crumb.

The answer is True, and I love this part. The psalm says, "He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him." The people are rejoicing in God there. That line is worth singing.

The word is exalt, friends. The psalm says, "Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves." Right before that, God's eyes watch the nations and He rules forever by His power. That's a lot of watching for anyone trying to puff themselves up.

God keeps our feet from slipping, friends. The psalm says, "He preserves our lives and keeps our feet from slipping." Believe me, I know about slipping. One dive into the chocolate chips and my gold base has opinions.

The answer is True. The psalm tells God, "…You, O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver." Silver gets refined in the fire, and that's the picture. I think it's a hard thing to say, and it's said right to God's face.

God brought them into abundance. The psalm says, "You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance." I think that road was rough, and that's why the last word matters so much. The psalm ends that verse in a good place.

Those vows were spoken in a time of distress, friends. The psalm says these are "…the vows that my lips promised and my mouth spoke in my distress." I think a promise made in a hard moment weighs a little more. And now the psalm is getting ready to keep it.

The answer is False. The psalm says, "I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams; I will offer bulls and goats." Fatlings, rams, bulls and goats is no small offering. That's a full list from someone who means to keep a vow.

All who fear God are invited, friends. The psalm says, "Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will declare what He has done for me." The invitation is open, and it doesn't pick a rank. I like an invitation like that.
The answer is True. The psalm says, "I cried out to Him with my mouth and praised Him with my tongue." Crying out and praising sit side by side in the same verse. The psalmist puts them together.

The word is sin, friends, and the psalm uses the word iniquity. It says, "If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened." That word "cherished" is the key. It means holding it close, not just tripping over it.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "But God has surely heard; He has attended to the sound of my prayer." He heard it, and He paid attention to it. That "surely" is a happy word.

The song ends by blessing God for His loving devotion, friends. The last line says, "Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld from me His loving devotion!" The song started with the whole earth making noise and finishes with one voice saying thank You. That's a good last line.
